title: Factors
subtitle: Find every factor of a number using factor pairs.

explanation.title: What is a factor?
paragraphs: A factor of a number divides it exactly, with no remainder.
3 × 4 = 12, so 3 and 4 are a factor pair of 12.
key_points: 1 and the number itself are always factors.

worked_examples.title: Factors come in pairs
steps: When the pairs meet in the middle, you have found them all.

interactive.title: Make equal rows
interactive.intro: Put 24 counters into equal rows. Every way that works gives a factor pair.

question_bank.title: Practise factors
question_bank.intro: Find factors, check exact division and recognise equal pairs.

questions.prompt: Which list contains every factor of 28?
questions.explanation: Pairs: 1 and 28, 2 and 14, 4 and 7. Test 3 and 5: both leave remainders. At 6, 28 ÷ 6 = 4 remainder 4. Since 6 is bigger than 4, stop. The factors are 1, 2, 4, 7, 14, 28.

questions.prompt: Sam says the factors of 16 are 1, 2, 8 and 16. What has he missed?
questions.explanation: Sam missed 4 because 4 × 4 = 16. Record the equal pair and list 4 once. The complete list is 1, 2, 4, 8, 16.

points.title: Find factors using equal rows.
points.text: If no counters are left over, the two numbers form a factor pair.

points.title: Find every pair.
points.text: Test the numbers in order until the pairs meet in the middle.

points.title: List each factor once.
points.text: For 16, the pair 4 × 4 gives just one 4 in the list.
